key_insight: ROGUE-AI finds that harmful agent behavior often stems from overlooked operational hazards rather than attacks, and hazard-specific warnings reduce harm.
engineering_relevance: Agent developers can use incident replications and matched controls as repeatable pre-release safety audits beyond prompt-injection testing.
method: Rebuild reported incidents offline using a multi-agent framework.
Compare agent behavior against matched controls lacking only the blamed cause.
Test hazard-specific warnings against same-length notes that omit the hazard.
evidence_signal: Across 108 attempted replications, ROGUE-AI reproduced reported harm in 89%; agents using five models made the reported mistake in 18–33% of runs versus at most 1% in matched controls.
watch_item: Offline reconstructions may not capture all production conditions, so replication results should not be treated as deployment-wide failure rates.
paper_title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
